problem:
Which of the following matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Matrices in Row Echelon Form
examples.problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/e300a9ac18f0170ae9053c9635fe13a9dd6def793ebfc0bd9dbe81e28810a347.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/f3d533c5687da1a75a07c6ad86b40ee8aa6ea5c86cdd250d5c47ff99b885ef61.png)

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/5d576fca72f6a4f9f0668ff0efbdc2cacc33f8dbb2c00192a7397da9ec83adea.png)

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/4f6a034def35760ae94b6eb6a425c59950556a78c124aa9ad0fcfdaa06053b28.png)

feedback.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $2$nd and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $2$nd and $4$th rows of  $A$ are $1$ and $3$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

So, the answer is $1+3=4.$
